llm.summary: This appears to be a real website-building scaffold, but it needs Review because its auth, payment, analytics, and deployment patterns are too sensitive and inconsistent to trust by default.

dimensions.detail: The full-stack website purpose is coherent, but the simple one-prompt site-builder framing understates high-impact capabilities such as live deployment, auth, payments, admin APIs, analytics, cron jobs, and multi-tenant state.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill includes confirmation checkpoints before deployment, migrations, production secrets, payments, and cron, but its triggers are broad and its manifest does not fully describe all sensitive credentials and operational behaviors used later.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No hidden installer, postinstall persistence, or automatic local execution was evident; deployment and npm publish scripts are visible and appear manually invoked.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: JWT, payment, AI, and database credentials are proportionate to the stated purpose, but the artifacts omit some required secrets and include weak or contradictory guidance for production secret handling.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill persists sessions, refresh tokens, analytics identifiers, chat history, orders, audit logs, and quotas; this is purpose-aligned, but token exposure, analytics consent gaps, logout/session handling, and destructive rollback guidance need review.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are prepared to review and harden the generated site before using real users, production data, payment credentials, AI API keys, or business accounts. Use a test EdgeOne project and sandbox credentials first, and specifically review auth/session handling, payment verification helpers, analytics consent, rollback migrations, and secret-management instructions before publishing.
llm.findings:
[SDI-4] unexpected: Confirmed several security-critical mismatches: the Edge middleware claims JWT protection but only forwards requests, login has a plaintext password comparison fallback, and token handling contradicts the HttpOnly-cookie security claims.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The payment package helper is presented as callback verification but accepts any parseable JSON as valid; the main WeChat callback is more hardened, so this is a production-readiness concern rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Broad triggers such as generic website-building requests are risky for a skill that can generate code, collect secrets, run migrations, and deploy infrastructure, even though later confirmation gates reduce the risk.
[SQP-2] expected: Analytics is a disclosed feature, but the client auto-initializes tracking and persists identifiers without a clear consent or opt-out enforcement path in the inspected code.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Login and refresh endpoints return access and refresh tokens in JSON and the client stores tokens in localStorage, weakening the stated HttpOnly-cookie model.
[E1] expected: External AI calls are expected for an AI chat module; the actual implementation currently uses a mock response, while reference examples still need clearer privacy and data-minimization guidance before production use.
[TM3] expected: Public-route allowlists are normal in auth middleware, but the documented skip-auth pattern should be reviewed carefully because future sensitive routes could be exposed if copied broadly.
[staticScan:suspicious.exposed_secret_literal] expected: The static scan's password-field findings appear to be false positives from reading login/register form values, not hardcoded secrets.
